ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Elvis Presley — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Ten-week review after the Las Vegas engagement and a back strain: buprenorphine, the taper, weight treatment, sleep apnea and planning for a three-week tour

text.paragraph: Ten-week review after the Las Vegas engagement and a back strain, before a three-week tour. [S]

Mr. Presley returns after a three-week engagement in Las Vegas and two weeks after the sick visit for a back strain. The back pain settled within a week on split buprenorphine doses and naproxen, and he has gone back to 16 mg once each morning. He took no other opioid and no extra diazepam. He had video visits in the first and third weeks of the engagement; the second was missed when a rehearsal ran late, and a nurse called him the next day. He used the travel CPAP on most nights. He has had mild nausea for a day after each tirzepatide dose and no constipation. His weight is 105.1 kg. His ophthalmologist saw him last week, found his eye pressures controlled on latanoprost and made no change. His HIV and hepatitis C tests were nonreactive and his hepatitis B tests showed no immunity. The tour begins in four days. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1974-09-23; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 126/80, pulse 74; weight 105.1 kg, BMI 31.4

Fatigue, weight gain of about 14 kg in two years, constipation with a bowel movement every five to seven days, loud snoring with daytime sleepiness, and high blood pressure readings, in a man taking two opioids, two benzodiazepines and an appetite suppressant from five prescribers; under evaluation with addiction medicine, a sleep study and home blood pressure readings
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented prescribed drugs and weight gain; superseded when the consultation and tests made the diagnoses.

Obesity, class 1 (BMI 32.5), with prediabetes (hemoglobin A1c 5.8%); recorded without stigma; weight gain began with long touring schedules, night eating after shows and an appetite suppressant that stopped working
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented weight gain.

Glaucoma secondary to steroids, both eyes, mild stage, after an acute angle-closure episode treated years ago; intraocular pressure controlled on latanoprost under his ophthalmologist; anticholinergic and sympathomimetic drugs to be avoided
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented glaucoma and the retrospective interpretation of it as steroid-induced; not a claim about his real eyes.

Opioid use disorder, severe, with prescription opioids from more than one prescriber (seven DSM-5-TR criteria, tolerance and withdrawal counted because the opioids were not taken as prescribed); on buprenorphine from the consultation; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented withdrawal from narcotic drugs and prescribed painkillers
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the addiction medicine consultation; person-first language; not a claim about his real diagnosis.

Sedative, hypnotic, or anxiolytic use disorder (benzodiazepines), moderate (five DSM-5-TR criteria), with two benzodiazepines from two prescribers; combined into diazepam and tapering slowly; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented prescribed sedatives
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation; not a claim about his real diagnosis.

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis confirmed with home readings, anchored to his documented hypertension.

S — Synthetic acute injury; not a historical claim.
